newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU plans further food safety measures.
newsitem.headline: EU plans further food safety measures.

text.p: The European Commission endorsed a call by Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler on Wednesday for further measures to protect consumers against mad cow disease.

Pressure for tougher action has grown following recent EU inspections showing that member states have not been respecting food safety rules to eliminate the disease, known as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).

"The EU's policy on BSE must continue to evolve in the light of experience and scientific knowledge with the primary objective of reducing the risk to human and animal health to as close to zero as possible," Fischler said in a statement.
Food Safety Commissioner Emma Bonino added that member states were responsible for implementing EU food safety rules.
British exports of gelatine made from British cattle parts would be made illegal pending new scientific evidence.
Specified risk material from cattle and sheep -- brains, eyes, spinal cord and spleen -- would be banned from all human and animal food.

Steps would be taken to ensure that new standards for processing meat and bone meal were respected by all EU member states. Infected meat and bonemeal mixed into cattle and sheep feed is believed to be the main cause of BSE.
Clarification that British re-exports of beef products imported into Britain were permitted.
The proposed extra measures will be examined by the EU's Standing Veterinary Committee of senior member state officials.
If there is a qualified majority in favour of the measures, they could then be approved by the Commission. If not, the issues would be referred to EU farm ministers.
